gloss: the above; the aforementioned; what is written above (or to the right)

definitions.gloss: the above; the aforementioned; what is written above (or to the right)
definitions.explanation: A formal reference to content written above or previously in a document, originating from vertical right-to-left writing where earlier content appears to the right.

examples.japanese: {右記|うき}の{通|とお}り{申請|しんせい}します。
{右記|うき}の{内容|ないよう}をご{確認|かくにん}ください。
{右記|うき}の{条件|じょうけん}に{同意|どうい}する{場合|ばあい}は{署名|しょめい}してください。
examples.english: If you agree to the conditions stated above, please sign.

notes:
{右|う} (right) + {記|き} (written). In traditional Japanese vertical writing, text flows from right to left, so earlier content is to the right. {右記|うき} therefore means "what was written previously" or "the above."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {右記|うき}の{通|とお}り: as stated above
- {右記|うき}の{住所|じゅうしょ}: the address listed above
- {右記|うき}の{条件|じょうけん}: the conditions stated above
- {右記|うき}のとおり{相違|そうい}ありません: the above is correct without error

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上記|じょうき}: the above — used in horizontal writing (modern standard); functionally equivalent
- {下記|かき}: the following, what is written below — the opposite, referring to content that comes after
- {左記|さき}: what follows (in vertical writing) — the counterpart to {右記|うき} in vertical text
- {前記|ぜんき}: the aforementioned — refers to content mentioned previously

USAGE:
{右記|うき} is used primarily in formal documents, legal papers, and official forms that use vertical writing. In modern horizontal writing, {上記|じょうき} is more common. Both are formal register.
